Global Genes is a leading rare disease patient advocacy organization founded in 2008, dedicated to connecting, empowering, and inspiring the rare disease community worldwide. In 2022, Global Genes merged with RARE-X to expand its research capabilities, now offering a collaborative data platform that enables global data sharing and analysis to accelerate treatments. The organization operates on a 'community of sharing' philosophy, with expert advisors from advocacy, research, and biopharma donating time and talent to support the rare disease community.

St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, founded by entertainer Danny Thomas in 1962, is a pediatric treatment and research facility headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee. The hospital's mission is to advance cures and means of prevention for pediatric catastrophic diseases through research and treatment. Approximately 90% of cancer patients at St. Jude are enrolled in research studies, ensuring that scientific discoveries translate directly into improved treatments.

Through St. Jude Global, the organization extends its impact worldwide, sharing knowledge, technology, and organizational skills to improve survival rates for children with cancer and other catastrophic diseases globally. St. Jude freely shares its research discoveries with the global healthcare and scientific communities, embodying its founder's vision that 'no child should die in the dawn of life.'

The foundation empowers everyone—from children hosting lemonade stands to major corporations—to make a difference in the fight against childhood cancer.

Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international medical humanitarian organization founded in 1971 by a group of French doctors and journalists. Operating in more than 70 countries, MSF provides emergency medical care to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, natural and human-made disasters, and exclusion from healthcare. With approximately 67,000 staff members of 169 nationalities, MSF delivers assistance based solely on need, irrespective of race, religion, gender, or political affiliation.

Beyond direct medical care, MSF conducts operational research to improve treatments, advocates for access to essential medicines through its Access Campaign, and bears witness to humanitarian crises through public testimony. MSF was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1999 for its pioneering humanitarian work and continues to push boundaries in global health response, including maritime search and rescue operations in the Mediterranean Sea.
